mainTopic: Why one may not insulate food in heat-adding material even before שבת, and the definition and halachic status of בין השמשות
overview: The amud opens at the end of a discussion about הטמנה, wrapping food to keep it hot. חז"ל forbade insulating in heat-adding material even before שבת. The reason is a chain of two גזירות: someone might insulate in ashes with a live coal, and then stir the coals on שבת. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא that says בין השמשות is a doubt, so the stringencies of both days apply to it. The ברייתא gives three definitions of twilight: רבי יהודה goes by the color of the sky, רבי נחמיה by the time to walk half a מיל, and רבי יוסי says it is only a blink of an eye. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע shows that 'the stringency of both days' matters for the laws of a זב who sees a discharge at twilight. Next, the גמרא notices that רבי יהודה's definition seems to contradict itself. רבה and רב יוסף resolve this in different ways, so רבה's בין השמשות is longer and רב יוסף's is shorter. Each one stays consistent in a second dispute about its length: רבה says three quarters of a מיל. רב יוסף says 'two parts of a מיל', and the explanation of that phrase continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why forbid heat-adding insulation even before שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why חז"ל forbade insulating food in a heat-adding material even while it is still day, before שבת begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the Sages say that one may not insulate food in something that adds heat, even while it is still daytime (before שבת)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a 'why' question about a known rule of הטמנה. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself is clear: you may not wrap food in a material that adds heat. What is puzzling is that the rule applies even before שבת, when cooking is fully allowed. So the question is about the reason behind such a broad ban.

keyTerms.meaning: insulating, wrapping food to keep it hot (הטמנה)
a material that adds heat, not just keeps heat in
while it is still day, before שבת starts

phrases.english: Why did they (the Sages) say
one may not insulate in something that adds heat
phrases.notes: Examples of such materials are hot ashes and manure.

phrases.english: and even while it is still day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of הטמנה on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the ban on heat-adding insulation applies even before שבת.

steps.title: A decree: he might insulate in ashes with live coals
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a גזירה: if heat-adding insulation were allowed, a person might insulate in ashes that still contain a burning coal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he will insulate in hot ashes that have a live coal in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered with a rabbinic safeguard (גזירה). People might not tell apart ordinary heat-adding materials from ashes with live coals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes with a live coal are a more serious case than other heat-adding materials. To stop people from reaching that case, חז"ל banned all heat-adding materials, even before שבת. At this point the answer does not yet say what is actually wrong with the ashes-and-coal case.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
hot ashes
a glowing, live coal

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he insulate
in hot ashes that have a live coal in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a גזירה, so that people do not come to insulate in ashes that contain a live coal.

steps.title: אביי: So what if he insulates in ashes with coals?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the answer: what is wrong with insulating in ashes that contain a coal?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: So let him insulate in them! (What is the problem?)
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back. The answer in step 2 assumed the ashes-and-coal case is forbidden, but it never explained why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה only makes sense if the thing it guards against is itself a problem. אביי points out that insulating in ashes with a coal is not obviously a violation. So the decree from step 2 still needs a real reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: he said to him (a direct challenge or reply)
so let him insulate! (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: So let him insulate!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question meaning: what is wrong with that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה that bans insulating out of concern for ashes with a coal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Insulating in ashes with a coal is not itself shown to be forbidden, so there is nothing yet for the decree to guard against.

steps.title: Second decree: he might stir the coals
steps.stepSummary: The reply is that the ashes-and-coal case is itself a גזירה: he might stir the coals on שבת to keep them burning, which is a Torah-level מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he will stir the coals.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to אביי reveals the real danger. Someone who insulates in live coals might stir them on שבת, which is the מלאכה of kindling (מבעיר).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full picture is a chain of two decrees. Heat-adding materials are banned because of ashes with a coal. Ashes with a coal are banned because one might stir the coals. The final link, stirring, is an actual Torah violation, so the whole chain rests on a real concern.

keyTerms.meaning: he will stir or rake (the coals), making them burn hotter
coals

steps.whatToRemember: Heat-adding insulation is banned even before שבת because of a two-step concern: insulating in ashes with live coals, and then stirring those coals on שבת.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he stir the coals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reveals a deeper underlying concern, forming a chain of decrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Insulating in ashes with a coal seemed harmless, which made the first decree look baseless.
steps.terutzMaskana: That case is itself forbidden, because the person might stir the coals on שבת, which is a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: Twilight is a doubt, so both days' stringencies apply
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that בין השמשות is a doubt: it may be part day and part night, all day, or all night. Therefore we apply the stringencies of both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Twilight is uncertain. It may be partly day and partly night, it may be entirely day, or it may be entirely night. So we apply to it the stringencies of both days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes a ברייתא about the status of בין השמשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three possibilities, and we cannot tell which one is true. So we treat twilight strictly as if it were part of whichever day makes it stricter. The ברייתא does not yet say which area of הלכה this affects. The גמרא asks about that in step 9, and steps 10-11 answer it: the laws of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
twilight, the period between sunset and nightfall
doubt, uncertainty
to the stringency of both days

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for every halachic question about twilight, such as when שבת begins and how days are counted.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת סָפֵק מִן הַיּוֹם וּמִן הַלַּיְלָה,
phrases.english: Twilight is a doubt: perhaps it is from the day and from the night,
perhaps it is entirely from the day,
perhaps it is entirely from the night —
we place upon it the stringency of both days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected to the משנה's theme of doubtful nightfall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בין השמשות is a doubt, so the stringencies of both the earlier and the later day apply to it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's definition of twilight by the color of the sky
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what twilight is. רבי יהודה answers: it starts at sunset and lasts while the sky is still reddish. Once the upper sky has lost its color and matches the lower sky, it is night.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is twilight? From when the sun sets, as long as the eastern face of the sky is reddish. If the lower part has turned pale and the upper part has not, it is twilight. If the upper part has turned pale and matches the lower part, it is night. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now defines the time period it just discussed. רבי יהודה gives a visual sign based on the sky's color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, twilight is a stretch of time you can see. It begins at sunset. It continues while some reddish color remains in the upper sky. Night arrives when the whole sky is the same pale color.

keyTerms.meaning: the sun sets
are reddish
turned pale, lost its color
became equal to, matched

phrases.english: And what is twilight?
From when the sun sets,
as long as the eastern face (of the sky) is reddish.
If the lower part turned pale and the upper part has not turned pale —
it is twilight.
If the upper part turned pale and matched the lower part —
that is night,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the period whose status was set out in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: twilight lasts from sunset until the upper sky loses its color and matches the lower sky.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: the time to walk half a מיל
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה measures twilight by time: as long as it takes a person to walk half a מיל after sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: The time it takes a person to walk half a מיל from when the sun sets.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא defines twilight with a fixed amount of time instead of a sign in the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה agrees that twilight is a real stretch of time after sunset. He disagrees about the measurement: he uses walking time, not the color of the sky.

keyTerms.meaning: the time it takes a person to walk
half a מיל, a distance used as a measure of time

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
the time it takes a person to walk
from when the sun sets, half a mil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different definition from רבי יהודה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נחמיה: twilight lasts the time it takes to walk half a מיל after sunset.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: twilight is just a blink of an eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that twilight is only an instant, the moment when night comes in and day goes out. It is too short to pin down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Twilight is like the blink of an eye. This one (night) comes in and that one (day) goes out, and it is impossible to pinpoint it.
steps.whatsHappening: The third opinion in the ברייתא says twilight is not a stretch of time at all, only a single moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה, twilight is a period you can measure. For רבי יוסי, it is only the point where day and night switch. It is so short that no one can identify it exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: like the blink of an eye
it is impossible to pinpoint it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יוסי with רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה gives a long, visible period. רבי יוסי says twilight is only an instant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
twilight is like the blink of an eye,
this one enters and that one leaves,
and it is impossible to pinpoint it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסִי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת כְּהֶרֶף עַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third definition, different from both earlier ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: twilight is an instant and cannot be pinpointed.

steps.title: Where does 'the stringency of both days' matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the line of the ברייתא saying that both days' stringencies apply, and asks which area of halacha this refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'We place upon it the stringency of both days.' For what הלכה does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא again so it can ask about its practical use. This sets up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a general rule but no example. The גמרא wants a concrete case where treating twilight as both days changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master said (quotes an earlier source in order to discuss it)
for what halacha? (what is the practical difference?)

phrases.english: The Master said:
we place upon it the stringency of both days.
phrases.notes: This repeats the ברייתא's line from step 5, now as the subject of a question.

phrases.english: For what halacha?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מְטִילִין אוֹתוֹ לְחוֹמֶר שְׁנֵי יָמִים. לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ruling in step 5, after the definitions in steps 6-8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which area of halacha the rule of 'the stringency of both days' applies to.

steps.title: רב הונא: it matters for טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the rule matters for the laws of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: It matters for טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא names the area of halacha where the twilight rule is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא points to טומאה as the practical example. His proof from a משנה comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: regarding ritual impurity

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
With regard to ritual impurity,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְעִנְיַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule applies to the laws of טומאה.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about a זב seeing at twilight
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a משנה about a זב who saw discharges during twilight. Because twilight might belong to either day, the sightings could count as more days than they seem, so we are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If he saw a discharge on two days during twilight, he is in doubt regarding טומאה and regarding a קרבן. If he saw on one day during twilight, he is in doubt regarding טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא backs up his answer with a משנה about a זב. The משנה shows twilight being treated as possibly belonging to two different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב who sees twice is fully טמא as a זב. One who sees three times must also bring a קרבן. Two twilight sightings could count as one, two, or three days, so he is in doubt about both טומאה and the קרבן. One twilight sighting could count as two days, so he is in doubt about טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned (in a משנה)
he saw (a discharge, as a זב)
an offering, which a זב brings after three sightings

steps.whatToRemember: 'The stringency of both days' means a twilight sighting can be counted toward both the day before and the day after. That is how a single sighting can make a זב doubtfully טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'saw two days' does not mean two days of daytime. It means two sightings, each one at twilight. That is what makes the number of days uncertain.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If he (a zav) saw on two days during twilight —
it is a doubt regarding impurity and regarding an offering.
If he saw on one day during twilight —
it is a doubt regarding impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן: רָאָה שְׁנֵי יָמִים בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's answer from step 10 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That 'the stringency of both days' applies to the laws of טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a זב who saw discharges during twilight, which treats twilight as possibly belonging to either day.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The first line of the ברייתא implies that once the lower sky turns pale it is night. A later line says that this same stage is בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא is itself difficult. You said: What is בין השמשות? From when the sun sets, as long as the eastern sky is red. That implies that if the lower part has turned pale and the upper part has not, it is already night. Yet the ברייתא then teaches: if the lower part turned pale and the upper part has not, it is בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two lines of the same ברייתא seem to clash about one stage of the evening sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line ties בין השמשות to the whole eastern sky being red. Once the lower part turns pale, the sky is no longer fully red, so this stage should already be night. The second line explicitly calls that same stage בין השמשות.

keyTerms.meaning: This (text) itself is difficult. It flags an internal contradiction.
Reddened (the sky glowing red after sunset)
Turned pale or silvery (lost its red color)
The lower / upper part of the eastern sky

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is an inference (הָא, 'implying'). The first line never says 'night' outright. The גמרא reads it from the time limit 'as long as it is red'.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult.
You said: what is twilight?
From when the sun sets,
as long as the eastern face of the sky is reddened.
Implying: if the lower part turned pale
and the upper part has not turned pale, it is night.
And then it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: הִכְסִיף הַתַּחְתּוֹן וְלֹא הִכְסִיף הָעֶלְיוֹן — בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: If the lower part turned pale and the upper did not, it is twilight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the טומאה application back to the wording of the ברייתא that defines בין השמשות
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא's definition of בין השמשות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause implies that the 'lower pale, upper red' stage is night. The second clause calls it בין השמשות.

steps.title: רבה: join both lines into one longer twilight
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, reads the two lines together. Both the full-red stage and the lower-pale stage are בין השמשות. Night begins only when the upper sky also turns pale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: Join the lines and teach them as one: What is בין השמשות? From sunset, as long as the eastern sky is red. And if the lower part turned pale but the upper did not, that is also בין השמשות. Once the upper part turns pale and matches the lower, it is night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה resolves the contradiction by treating the second line as an extension of the first, not as a clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, 'as long as it is red' does not mean that night begins when the redness starts to fade. The lower-pale stage is added on as more בין השמשות. So בין השמשות runs from sunset until the whole sky is pale, which makes it a fairly long period.

keyTerms.meaning: Join (the lines together) and teach them as one
Also
And it became equal to the lower part (the whole sky is uniformly pale)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Join them together and teach:
What is twilight?

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁתִּשְׁקַע הַחַמָּה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁפְּנֵי מִזְרָח מַאֲדִימִין.
phrases.english: From when the sun sets, as long as the eastern face is reddened.
And if the lower turned pale and the upper did not,
it is also twilight.
If the upper turned pale and equaled the lower, it is night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the two clauses are combined into one continuous definition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause implies that night begins as soon as the redness fades at the bottom
steps.terutzMaskana: The red stage and the lower-pale stage are both בין השמשות; night begins only when the whole sky is pale

steps.title: רב יוסף: the red stage is still day
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, quoting the same chain of teachers, reads the ברייתא as three stages. While the sky is red it is still day. The lower-pale stage is בין השמשות. When the whole sky is pale it is night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: This is what the ברייתא is teaching. From sunset, as long as the eastern sky is red, it is day. If the lower part turned pale and the upper did not, it is בין השמשות. If the upper part turned pale and matched the lower, it is night.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a different fix. He reads the first line as describing day, not בין השמשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יוסף, the red stage after sunset is still fully day. Only the lower-pale stage counts as בין השמשות, so the contradiction disappears. His בין השמשות is therefore shorter than רבה's.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching (a rereading of the text)
Day

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: red stage plus lower-pale stage are both בין השמשות, so it is long. רב יוסף: red stage is day and only the lower-pale stage is בין השמשות, so it is short.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said,
this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁתִּשְׁקַע הַחַמָּה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁפְּנֵי מִזְרָח מַאֲדִימִין — יוֹם.
phrases.english: From when the sun sets, as long as the eastern face is reddened, it is day.

phrases.aramaic: הִכְסִיף הַתַּחְתּוֹן וְלֹא הִכְסִיף הָעֶלְיוֹן — בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: If the lower turned pale and the upper did not, it is twilight.
If the upper turned pale and equaled the lower, it is night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second resolution of the same contradiction, competing with רבה's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the first clause defines day, not בין השמשות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause defines בין השמשות
steps.terutzMaskana: Red sky means day, lower-pale means בין השמשות, and fully pale means night

steps.title: Each follows his own view: how long is twilight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבה and רב יוסף are each consistent with another statement of theirs. It opens that statement with the question of how long בין השמשות lasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they each follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: How long is the measure of בין השמשות?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to show that רבה and רב יוסף also disagree about how long בין השמשות lasts, and that this matches their readings of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reading made בין השמשות longer and רב יוסף's made it shorter. The גמרא now brings a separate dispute about its length to show that each one is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: And they follow their own reasoning (each one is consistent with his view elsewhere)
As it was stated (by אמוראים)
Measure, amount

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as it was stated: How long is the measure of twilight?

steps.title: רבה: three parts of a מיל
steps.stepSummary: רבה, in the name of רב יהודה and שמואל, says that בין השמשות lasts as long as it takes to walk three parts of a מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: three parts of a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his length for בין השמשות, measured in walking time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Time is measured by how long it takes to walk a distance, just as רבי נחמיה did earlier with half a מיל. The phrase 'three parts' is unclear, so the גמרא will define it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A distance of 2,000 אמות; here it stands for the time it takes to walk that distance

steps.title: What does 'three parts' mean? Two options rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'three parts of a מיל' means. Three halves would be said as 'a מיל and a half', and three thirds would be said as 'a מיל', so neither can be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'three parts of a מיל'? If you say three halves of a מיל, let him say 'a מיל and a half'. Rather, if it means three thirds of a מיל, let him just say 'a מיל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies רבה's unclear phrase by ruling out readings that would have been stated more simply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of thumb is that a teacher would not use a roundabout phrase when a simple one exists. Three halves equals one and a half, and three thirds equals one whole. So 'parts' must mean some other fraction.

steps.title: It means three-quarters of a מיל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'three parts' means three quarters of a מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: three quarters of a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting halves and thirds, the גמרא settles on quarters. רבה's בין השמשות is three-quarters of a מיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three quarters cannot be said more simply, so this reading fits the wording. It is a relatively long period, which matches רבה's view that both the red stage and the lower-pale stage count as בין השמשות.

keyTerms.meaning: Quarters

phrases.english: Rather: three quarters of a mil.

steps.title: רב יוסף: two parts of a מיל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, quoting the same chain, says that בין השמשות lasts two parts of a מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: two parts of a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his own, shorter length for בין השמשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב יוסף counts only the lower-pale stage as בין השמשות, we expect a shorter time than רבה's. Again the wording 'two parts' needs to be defined.

steps.title: What does 'two parts' mean? Two options rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'two parts of a מיל' means. Two halves would be said as 'a מיל', and two quarters would be said as 'half a מיל'. This passage ends as the גמרא begins its answer with 'Rather'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'two parts of a מיל'? If you say two halves of a מיל, let him say 'a מיל'. And if it means two quarters of a מיל, let him say 'half a מיל'. Rather...
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same method as before, the גמרא rules out halves and quarters. The answer begins at the end of the amud and continues in the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two halves equals one whole, and two quarters equals one half, so neither fits the roundabout wording. The final 'אֶלָּא' introduces the correct fraction, which comes on the next amud.
